excerpt:
Barker is the second court in as many months to invalidate an employee non-solicitation provision and employers who regularly include such provisions in their agreements with California employees should reassess their use and enforcement of those provisions.

In doing so, the Court adopted the primary holding of AMN – that contractual prohibitions barring solicitation of employees are invalid under the California Supreme Court's reasoning in Edwards v. Arthur Andersen LLP (2008) 44 Cal. 4th 937. The Court also rejected the secondary ruling in AMN, which would have arguably limited the holding
